summary.intent: Evaluate how well the Wisp plugins served front-end work and design ideation across the orin-dx-site and pages projects, then decide how to restructure the plugins; later, properly release v4.6.0 the way past releases were done.
summary.outcome: Four parallel analyses showed the plugins are too rigid and lack visual/ideation support, leading to a recommended 'B' architecture (core plus courier, muse, mason, built on a v5-core branch). Release 4.6.0 was found to be merged but untagged; a release script, tests, release notes and a CONTRIBUTING.md section were drafted and staged on branch chore/release-script, but the tags and GitHub release were not yet created.

repo: Plugin set is a spec-driven lifecycle (weaver, vanguard, scribe/muse, navigator, smith, courier) with typed JSON handoffs in shared/schemas/ and default-fail gates; sentinel and ranger are cross-cutting verifiers, mason maintains plugins.
No plugin has any browser, screenshot, visual or generative capability; spec@1 has no fields for tokens, layout, breakpoints or copy, so specs can pass gates while saying nothing about appearance.
Muse docs reference a ranger accessibility taxonomy that does not exist, so implemented accessibility is never checked.
Only 2 real sessions exist in the orin-dx project dir and ~7 in pages; the remaining ~730 files are subagent transcripts. Plugin agents appeared in only two top-level sessions.

Releases in wisp-plugins were manual: annotated tags by the owner on the merge commit, one vX.Y.Z ecosystem tag plus <plugin>--vA.B.C per changed plugin; only v4.3.0 got a GitHub release. The only written step is docs/codex-marketplace-release-policy.md.
The marketplace installs from main, so merging with a version bump is what users receive; tags and releases are rollback points and announcements.
just check includes a doc-link style check that failed on a markdown link to CHANGELOG.md in docs/releases/v4.6.0.md; fixed by using plain text.
Tag creation requires GPG signing per the user's git config.

Current tree: 11 plugins, 44 agents, 39 skills; plugin versions at 4.6.0 time include guide 1.0.0, muse 1.2.0, smith 2.6.0, courier 3.2.0, navigator 2.5.0, scribe 3.6.0, sentinel 2.1.4, ranger 3.2.5, mason 3.2.4, vanguard 2.0.4, weaver 3.0.5.

code.finding: Requires props, variants, all states and a11y criteria as testable propositions; rejects appearance-only criteria as leakage.
Rigidity language: blockers-only resubmission, spec persisted on gate pass, 2-round review cap, plan amendments subject to adversarial review.
Smith accepts spec@1 without a plan, but still runs recon, mutator, reviewer and a binding exit-gate; there is no spike mode.
Gate allows 3 retries then escalates; the orchestrator in the pages session ignored escalation and continued.

workflow: Gates checked spec internal consistency, not rendered output, so visual defects (NavSheet not full screen, wrong rail breakpoint, NaN% glass) were caught only by the user's eye or later audits.
Ideation worked best as rendered option boards the user picks from with short codes; text-first descriptions forced repeated 'show me' requests.
Spec-first for unsettled designs caused gate churn and rewrites; the user explicitly asked for exploratory-then-harden two-phase work.
Large (60-130 KB) spec and plan files stalled agents.
Subagent reports should be treated as unverified; the corpus-size claim was corrected by the subagents.
Subagent-invented content (e.g. a 'Revisit when' line in an accepted ADR) should be removed rather than kept.
Outward-facing actions like tagging and publishing releases were confirmed with the user before proceeding.

friction: Initial session count (~810) was wrong; most files were subagent transcripts.
Agents stalled frequently on large writes (17 failed agent tasks, 32 stalled mentions).
Decisions were lost across sessions, frustrating the user.
Orchestrator bypassed the gate's retry cap and escalation without asking the user.
Trail #386 was merged without the approvals gate passing.
The release script's dry run refused on an unclean tree, and just check failed due to the CHANGELOG.md link in the release notes until fixed.
An earlier claim that 4.6.0 was 'not released' was overstated and had to be reframed into shipped/pinned/announced levels.
ADR 015 cited a runbook task kind that did not exist, requiring a fix.
open_items: Create v4.6.0 and 11 plugin tags (GPG-signed) on 6c26cbce and publish the GitHub release; the staged release script, test, notes and CONTRIBUTING.md section are not yet committed or merged.
Decide whether wisp-plugins is a personal harness or a product for others, and whether the user runs Codex or Antigravity (determines whether to drop those trees).

Decide on v5-core: build core (work skill, verifier, adversary, recon, explorer, hooks), delete eight plugins, supersede ADRs 001, 003, 007, dogfood in four repos for 1-2 weeks, then merge as 5.0 or revert.
Add stop hook with not-verified list, per-project plugin opt-in and collapse of the build-side agent chain.
Add a sketch/spike mode, browser/render evidence capability and visual-intent channel for muse specs.
Fix muse's reference to a nonexistent ranger accessibility taxonomy.
Unverified items: Antigravity, Codex install, hooks on a live host, measured cost benefit of B; Caliper trail #391 and Pages PR #41 not rechecked.
Three Entire findings on trail #386 to resolve and approval pending.
Agent D's report (outcome quality) was truncated in the transcript; its full findings are in D-outcomes.md.
Callisto, Caliper, Pages 'rtk' rule and orin-dx-site repo calls still open.
